title: Revalidation
definition: The process of purging the Next.js Data Cache and re-fetching fresh data.
simpleExplanation: Next.js caches your fetch requests to make your site fast. But if you update a blog post, the cache is now wrong. Revalidation is how you tell Next.js: 'Hey, throw away that old cached version and grab the new one.'
realWorldExample: Time-based: Revalidating a 'Live Weather' API every 60 seconds. On-demand: Revalidating the 'Products' page the exact millisecond an admin clicks 'Save' in the CMS.

basic: What are the two main types of revalidation in Next.js?
intermediate: If you set `revalidate: 3600`, how often does the data refresh?

answers.question: Two types?
answers.answer: 1. Time-based (Background revalidation every X seconds). 2. On-demand (Triggered manually via an API route or Server Action).

answers.question: How often?
answers.answer: Every 3,600 seconds (1 hour). Next.js will serve the cached version for an hour, and then rebuild it in the background on the next request.
